text: The discipline this chapter proposes has two halves: ___ to predict how a program scales, and measure to know what it costs.
explanation: Both, for different questions. Analysis without measurement produces programs optimized for the wrong constant; measurement without analysis produces programs that pass every test and fail when the data grows. A measurement at n = 1000 tells you nothing about n = 10⁶, and no amount of profiling today reveals that an O(n²) method fine on today's data will not survive next year's.
